# Glossary {#sec-glossary .unnumbered}

This glossary defines key terms used throughout *Physical AI*. Terms are organized alphabetically.

```{=latex}
\small\sloppy
\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
\setlist[description]{
  style=unboxed,
```

## A {#sec-glossary-vol4-a .unlisted}

**Action Chunk Seam Discontinuity**
: A kinematic boundary mismatch where one admitted action chunk meets the next with discontinuous position, velocity, or acceleration. An unmanaged step in velocity implies an infinite acceleration impulse, while an acceleration step requests an instantaneous torque step bounded by plant actuator bandwidth and drive compliance. Mitigated by $C^2$ jerk-continuous Hermite or quintic spline seams and receding-horizon temporal ensembling. (@Sec-planning, @sec-appendix-control-splines)

**Action Chunking (Temporal Action Chunking)**
: A policy inference strategy that outputs an open-loop sequence of $K$ consecutive future actions $\mathbf{a}_{t:t+K-1}$ from a single observation or latent state. Reduces effective policy query frequency to match slow neural network inference latencies while dampening compounding closed-loop covariate shift. Requires overlapping receding-horizon execution or temporal ensembling to maintain closed-loop responsiveness to dynamic environmental disturbances. (@Sec-brain, @sec-planning, @sec-training)

**Actuator Authority Budget**
: The bounded set of admissible generalized forces, torques, and accelerations that a physical actuation system can deliver without violating electrical, thermal, or mechanical limits. Defined by the intersection of peak motor torque $\tau_{\text{peak}}$, continuous thermal torque $\tau_{\text{cont}}$, DC bus voltage limits, inverter current ratings, and transmission gear constraints. Any proposed trajectory whose required joint torques exceed this budget induces tracking saturation and loss of control authority. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-actuators)

**Actuator Thermal Duty Cycle ($D$)**
: The dimensionless fraction of operational time during which an actuator operates under peak torque relative to continuous cooling intervals: $D = t_{\text{on}} / (t_{\text{on}} + t_{\text{off}})$. Governs winding temperature rise according to Joule heating ($P_{\text{loss}} = I^2 R$) and thermal dissipation time constants. Exceeding the allowable duty cycle triggers thermal foldback protection, attenuating available torque and compromising dynamic braking capacity. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-actuators)

**Adversarial Safety Defeater**
: A targeted environmental perturbation, sensor artifact, or distribution shift structured to bypass learned or heuristic safety filters while maintaining nominal execution metrics. Exploits epistemic blind spots in high-dimensional perception models to induce silent unshielded hazard proposals. Defeated only through independent, physically grounded supervisory guards and formal barrier certificates. (@Sec-release, @sec-frontier)

**Affordance Grounding Envelope**
: The spatial and kinematic region surrounding an object within which an end-effector can successfully initiate, maintain, and complete a specified physical manipulation primitive. Combines geometric reachable workspace with contact stability margins and surface friction cones. Grounding failures occur when high-level semantic tokens designate affordances outside the kinematically reachable and force-feasible envelope. (@Sec-intent, @sec-appendix-control-reachability)

**Arithmetic Intensity in Embodied Inference ($I$)**
: The ratio of floating-point operations performed to bytes of memory transferred from off-chip storage during model inference: $I = \text{FLOPs} / \text{Bytes}$. Determines whether an on-device neural policy is compute-bound or memory-bandwidth-bound on an embedded system-on-chip. Autoregressive generation at batch size 1 exhibits low arithmetic intensity, causing memory bandwidth saturation and tail latency inflation. (@Sec-brain, @sec-placement)

**Asymmetric Multiprocessing (AMP)**
: A system-on-chip execution architecture where cores of different architectures and privilege levels execute independent operating systems without shared scheduling. Pairs high-throughput application processors running Linux for perception and planning with isolated, deterministic real-time microcontrollers executing safety-critical bare-metal motor control loops. Communicates across hardware boundaries via lock-free shared memory mailboxes. (@Sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-ipc)

**Astronomical Exposure Wall (Butler & Finelli Bound)**
: A statistical fundamental limit governing the empirical validation of ultra-reliable autonomous systems. Under a stationary Poisson failure model, establishing a failure rate upper bound $\lambda \le 10^{-9}$ per machine-hour at 95 percent confidence requires demonstrating at least $-\ln(0.05)/\lambda \approx 3.0 \times 10^9$ failure-free operating hours. Demonstrating ultra-reliability purely through statistical black-box road or bench testing is infeasible, necessitating deterministic architectural safety guarantees, formal verification, and conservative invariant monitoring. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-verification, @sec-frontier, @sec-appendix-ml-exposure)

**Autoregressive Generation Latency**
: The serial inference delay incurred when a neural sequence model or vision-language-action policy predicts future tokens or actions one step at a time. Each generated step requires a full forward pass through transformer layers, binding execution speed to memory bandwidth limits. Creates substantial physical phase lag when high-level planners attempt to govern dynamic, high-bandwidth contact tasks. (@Sec-brain, @sec-intent)

## B {#sec-glossary-vol4-b .unlisted}

**Back-Electromotive Force (Back-EMF, $e_{\text{bemf}}$)**
: An internal counter-voltage generated across electric motor windings as the permanent-magnet rotor rotates through the stator magnetic field: $e_{\text{bemf}} = K_e \dot{\theta}_m$. Opposes supply bus voltage and limits maximum attainable rotor velocity according to $\omega_{\text{max}} \le (V_{\text{bus}} - I R) / K_e$. Imposes an absolute physical boundary on high-speed dynamic braking and rapid evasive trajectory maneuvers. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-actuators)

**Behavioral Cloning Horizon Bound**
: A theoretical bound characterizing quadratic compounding error growth in open-loop imitation learning. If a policy incurs an expected per-step single-action discrepancy $\epsilon$ relative to expert demonstrations, the expected trajectory deviation after $T$ steps scales as $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon T^2)$ under arbitrary transitions. In physical systems, this quadratic drift drives the robot out of the demonstration support manifold into unrecoverable crash states. (@Sec-training, @sec-appendix-ml-compounding)

**Belief State Invalidation Horizon ($t_{\text{exp}}$)**
: The elapsed temporal duration beyond which a physical state estimate no longer satisfies its certified spatial accuracy bound. Evaluated from disturbance growth laws, unmodeled obstacle velocities, and sensor noise propagation: $t_{\text{exp}} = \sup \{ t \mid \mathbb{P}(\|x(t) - \hat{x}(t)\| \le \delta) \ge 1 - \alpha \}$. Requires that spatial representations expire dynamically to prevent collision checks from evaluating stale free space. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-control-covariance)

**Bilateral Teleoperation Scattering Matrix**
: A frequency-domain representation characterizing power transmission and reflection across a delayed communication channel between master and slave manipulators. Used in passivity analysis to ensure that communication time delays do not generate spurious physical energy that would destabilize coupled human-robot feedback dynamics. (@Sec-data, @sec-appendix-control-passivity)

**Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) Metric Representation**
: An orthographic, top-down spatial coordinate frame in which multi-camera and sensor features are explicitly projected onto a metric ground plane. Eliminates perspective foreshortening and scale ambiguity present in raw perspective camera frames, providing a physically consistent substrate for motion planning and barrier evaluation. (@Sec-perception, @sec-appendix-ml-patch-embedding)

**Bumpless Authority Transfer Ramp ($C^2$)**
: A smooth arbitration mechanism that transitions actuation authority between human teleoperator and autonomous policy without introducing torque shocks. Employs a twice-continuously differentiable blending function $\sigma(t) \in [0, 1]$ such that $\dot{\sigma}(0) = \dot{\sigma}(T) = \ddot{\sigma}(0) = \ddot{\sigma}(T) = 0$. Eliminates step changes in commanded acceleration that would otherwise excite high-frequency structural resonances or trip inverter overcurrent protections. (@Sec-intervention, @sec-appendix-control-splines)

## C {#sec-glossary-vol4-c .unlisted}

**Camera-to-IMU Spatial-Temporal Calibration**
: The joint estimation of rigid six-degree-of-freedom coordinate transforms and temporal phase offsets between visual optical centers and inertial measurement units. Solves for rotation $\mathbf{R}_{c}^{b}$, translation $\mathbf{p}_{c}^{b}$, and clock latency offset $\Delta t_{\text{sync}}$ by minimizing joint photometric and inertial re-projection residuals. Calibration drift on the order of milliseconds induces false angular acceleration estimates, degrading visual-inertial odometry stability. (@Sec-perception, @sec-appendix-systems-vision)

**CAN FD Bus Arbitration and Bit Stuffing**
: A deterministic industrial bus protocol feature providing prioritized message arbitration and cyclic redundancy checks at flexible data rates up to $8\,\text{Mbps}$. Dominant-bit arbitration guarantees that highest-priority safety messages transmit without backoff or collisions, while bit stuffing maintains physical clock synchronization across transceiver nodes. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-appendix-systems-fieldbus)

**Capability Matrix**
: An online lookup structure mapping current operational states and hardware health metrics to admitted control actions and safe fallback modes. Maintains verified system invariants across degraded sub-states such as sensor packet loss, bus voltage droop, or thermal throttling. Restricts proposed high-performance policies from executing maneuvers beyond current physical health boundaries. (@Sec-intervention, @sec-release)

**Category 0 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**
: An uncontrolled emergency stop executed by immediate, unconditioned removal of electrical power from all actuator drives. Actuators coast freely or engage unpowered electromechanical holding brakes under safe torque off. Selected only when unpowered coasting or mechanical friction stops the system within available clearance margins faster or more safely than controlled electrical deceleration. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-body)

**Category 1 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**
: A controlled emergency stop that maintains electrical power to actuator drives during active deceleration until zero velocity is verified, after which power is removed. Maximizes deceleration rate within inverter dynamic braking limits before engaging holding brakes. Prevents uncontrolled kinematic flailing or jackknifing in articulated manipulators and multi-link mobile bases. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-body)

**Category 2 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**
: A controlled operational stop where actuator drives decelerate the machine to zero velocity and remain powered to hold position actively. Retains full motor torque to resist external gravity loads, active payloads, or environmental forces without engaging mechanical wear brakes. Requires independent supervisor monitoring to ensure the active hold does not drift. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-body)

**Causal Boundary**
: The physical and architectural dividing line separating reversible computational proposal generation from irreversible physical actuation. Once energy transfers from power electronics into actuators, physical work is performed on the environment ($dW = \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{x}$), establishing permanent real-world consequences that cannot be undone by software rollbacks or exception handlers. Defines the exact placement of safety enforcement filters. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-body)

**Causal Misidentification (Causal Confusion in Policy Learning)**
: An imitation learning failure where a policy conditions on spurious, non-causal features that correlate with expert actions in training demonstrations. Occurs when high-capacity neural networks exploit incidental environmental indicators (such as visual interface indicators, sensor glare, or past actions) rather than true task affordances. Deployed closed-loop policies catastrophically fail when test-time interventions alter non-causal correlations. (@Sec-training)

**Censored Trial Fallacy (Denominator Filtering)**
: An evaluation bias that understates autonomous failure rates by excluding aborted, intervened, or out-of-boundary runs from the statistical denominator. When human safety drivers or runtime supervisors intervene to prevent imminent physical collisions, treating the aborted trials as invalid runs inflates apparent autonomous reliability metrics. Every supervisory intervention must be formally logged as a counterfactual failure event unless independently proven safe. (@Sec-evaluation)

**Centroidal Dynamics**
: A reduced-order physical model projecting the full multi-body dynamics of articulated mobile robots onto the motion of their center of mass and total angular momentum: $\dot{\mathbf{p}}_{\text{com}} = \sum \mathbf{f}_i + m\mathbf{g}$ and $\dot{\mathbf{L}}_{\text{com}} = \sum (\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{p}_{\text{com}}) \times \mathbf{f}_i$. Enables tractable, real-time quadratic programming for floating-base whole-body locomotion and dynamic balancing. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-control-centroidal)

**Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE)**
: A structured assurance framework establishing an explicit, auditable argument that a cyber-physical system satisfies its safety requirements within an operational design domain. Organizes safety claims hierarchically, linking high-level goals to concrete technical arguments and empirically validated verification evidence including fault injection records, hardware-in-the-loop stress tests, and formal invariance proofs. (@Sec-release)

**Clearance Inset Margin ($C_{\text{inset}}$)**
: A geometric buffer added to robot boundary contours to absorb spatial perception inaccuracies, odometry drift, and mechanical tracking tolerances. Ensures that nominal path planning treats obstacle boundaries conservatively: $d_{\text{safe}} = d_{\text{obs}} + C_{\text{inset}}$, where $C_{\text{inset}} \ge 3\sigma_{\text{pos}} + v_{\text{max}}\tau_{\text{latency}}$. Prevents micro-collisions caused by unmodeled structural flexure or sensor quantization. (@Sec-perception, @sec-planning)

**Clopper-Pearson Exact Confidence Interval**
: A non-asymptotic statistical interval providing exact binomial coverage guarantees for physical safety validation. Computes exact upper and lower failure probability bounds without relying on Gaussian approximations, ensuring valid coverage even when zero failures are observed across $N$ physical trials: $\theta_{\text{upper}} = 1 - (1 - c)^{1/N}$ at confidence level $c$. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-appendix-ml-exposure)

**Closed-Loop Evaluation Estimand**
: The true, underlying statistical expectation of task success or safety violation rate under closed-loop rollout dynamics: $J(\pi) = \mathbb{E}_{\tau \sim p_\pi}[R(\tau)]$. Fundamentally distinct from static dataset loss metrics because the deployed policy generates its own future state distribution through physical feedback. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-appendix-ml-trajectory-distribution)

**Compounding Rollout Error**
: The cumulative drift between an autonomous policy's closed-loop trajectory distribution and the demonstration distribution across time. Small open-loop prediction errors perturb the agent into novel states with higher downstream epistemic uncertainty, precipitating further errors and rapid trajectory divergence. Bounded only through closed-loop feedback, active domain randomization, or external barrier shielding. (@Sec-training, @sec-appendix-ml-compounding)

**Control Barrier Function (CBF-QP) Safety Filter**
: A real-time optimization filter that projects candidate control proposals onto the half-space of forward-invariant safe inputs. Given a continuously differentiable scalar barrier function $h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$, enforces the Nagumo-type condition $\dot{h}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u}) + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0$ at high loop rates via a quadratic program: $\mathbf{u}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{u}} \|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{u}_{\text{prop}}\|^2$ subject to linear barrier constraints. Guarantees safety while maximally preserving nominal policy performance. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf)

**Cross-Class Coupled Contention**
: System-on-chip interconnect interference where high-bandwidth, non-critical background traffic degrades hard real-time motor control loops. Occurs when bulk direct memory access transfers (such as neural network weight streaming or camera frame ingestion) saturate shared crossbar switches or memory controllers, inflating the worst-case execution time of microsecond-critical supervisor interrupts. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-dram)

**Cross-Embodiment Compatibility Contract**
: A formal specification defining the kinematic, dynamic, and latency invariants required to transfer learned manipulation or locomotion policies across distinct physical robot embodiments. Normalizes joint limits, torque-speed curves, sensor mounting transforms, and loop frequencies. Verifies that candidate policies do not demand accelerations or bandwidths exceeding the target embodiment's physical limits. (@Sec-data)

**Cryptographic Release Manifest**
: An immutable, digitally signed hardware-and-software record detailing every qualified component deployed in a physical AI system. Binds model weights, microcontroller firmware hashes, sensor calibration matrices, and safety case verdicts into a signed ledger verified at boot time. Prevents uncertified firmware combinations from commanding actuator power electronics. (@Sec-release)

**Cyclic Synchronous Position (CSP) Mode**
: A standardized industrial drive control mode (CiA 402) where a centralized motion controller periodically transmits target position setpoints to motor inverters over a deterministic fieldbus at fixed intervals. The drive's internal closed-loop controllers interpolate intermediate trajectory points, executing current and velocity loops locally at multi-kilohertz frequencies. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-appendix-systems-fieldbus)

## D {#sec-glossary-vol4-d .unlisted}

**DC Bus Transient Voltage Droop ($\Delta V_{\text{droop}}$)**
: An instantaneous supply rail voltage dip caused by high transient current demands across finite power distribution network impedance: $\Delta V = L \frac{di}{dt} + R i$. Induced by simultaneous peak torque commands or high-power compute bursts. If bus voltage drops below microcontroller brownout thresholds, processors reset mid-maneuver, triggering sudden actuator power dropouts. (@Sec-body, @sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-droop)

**Demonstration Provenance Tuple**
: A four-stream logging protocol $(a_{\text{req}}, a_{\text{cmd}}, a_{\text{enf}}, a_{\text{meas}})$ that captures the complete physical lifecycle of an action during data collection. Distinguishes raw operator intent ($a_{\text{req}}$), kinematically transformed setpoints ($a_{\text{cmd}}$), safety-governor clamped commands ($a_{\text{enf}}$), and actual plant response ($a_{\text{meas}}$). Prevents policy training from mistaking intervention clamps or structural backlash for intended human behavior. (@Sec-data)

**Deterministic Fieldbus**
: A digital industrial communication bus providing mathematically bounded transmission latency and zero packet loss for real-time control loops. Implemented via protocols such as EtherCAT or CAN FD with cyclic synchronous positioning. Enforces strict time-triggered message scheduling to prevent jitter in multi-axis motor synchronization. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-appendix-systems-fieldbus)

**Detectorless Failure Mode**
: A catastrophic hazard mechanism for which on-board sensors provide no timely distinguishing observation before the physical intervention deadline expires. Examples include micro-fractures in structural titanium, subterranean soil collapse beneath treads, or instantaneous optical sensor blinding by direct laser strikes. Mitigated exclusively through passive structural design, conservative operational design domains, or scheduled non-destructive inspection. (@Sec-frontier)

**Differential Flatness in Trajectory Tracking**
: A geometric property of certain nonlinear dynamic systems allowing all state and input variables to be determined algebraically from a set of flat outputs and their time derivatives without numerical integration. Allows rapid generation of dynamically feasible, constraint-satisfying trajectories for quadrotors and nonholonomic wheeled robots. (@Sec-planning, @sec-appendix-control-splines)

**Diffusion Policy**
: A continuous trajectory generation policy that models multi-modal action distributions by inverting a stochastic diffusion process. Learns the score function $\nabla_{\mathbf{a}} \log p(\mathbf{a} \mid \mathbf{o})$, generating smoothed action chunks by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise conditioned on sensor embeddings. Successfully handles multi-modal demonstrations without collapsing into dangerous mode averaging. (@Sec-training, @sec-appendix-ml-diffusion)

**Domain Randomization Corridor**
: The bounded parametric interval across physical parameters (mass, friction, damping, latency) used during simulation training to bridge the reality gap. Calibrated to ensure that the physical world lies within the convex hull of randomized simulated environments without expanding variance so broadly that policy capacity or optimality degrades. (@Sec-training)

**DRAM Contention Tail Latency**
: The maximum execution delay incurred when concurrent CPU, GPU, and direct memory access requests collide at shared dynamic RAM controllers. Caused by row-buffer misses, bank conflicts, and bus turnaround cycles on integrated heterogeneous system-on-chip silicon. Expands memory access times by up to an order of magnitude, jeopardizing real-time control deadlines unless bounded by memory channel partitioning or cache locking. (@Sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-dram)

**Dynamic Braking Chopper Resistor**
: A dedicated power resistor and switching transistor connected across an electric drive's DC bus to dissipate excess kinetic energy during aggressive deceleration. Prevents bus overvoltage conditions when regenerative motor currents exceed the absorption capacity of the battery or power supply. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-power)

**Dynamic Fallback Ladder (Minimal Risk Maneuver)**
: A prioritized hierarchy of deterministically validated safety responses executed by an independent supervisor when nominal tracking fails. Sequences through command filtering, $C^2$ deceleration to stop, active powered hold, and mechanical brake engagement (Category 1/0 stop). Selected dynamically based on plant health, remaining stopping distance, and ground-truth velocity. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-intervention)

**Dynamic Obstacle Velocity Cone**
: A geometric construct mapping the relative positions and velocities of moving environmental obstacles into the set of robot velocities that would lead to collision within a finite horizon. Enables velocity obstacle planners to synthesize evasive maneuvers around dynamic pedestrians and co-located machinery. (@Sec-planning)

**Dynamic Reachability Envelope ($\mathcal{R}(\tau)$)**
: The set of all Cartesian positions and joint configurations reachable by a physical embodiment within time horizon $\tau$ under current kinematic and dynamic constraints. Explicitly incorporates velocity limits, torque-speed curves, and payload inertia. High-level task planners evaluate reachability envelopes to reject infeasible goal assignments prior to trajectory generation. (@Sec-intent, @sec-appendix-control-reachability)

**Dynamic Stopping Distance ($d_{\text{stop}}$)**
: The certified physical distance required to bring a moving system to a complete standstill from its current velocity: $d_{\text{stop}} = v \tau_{\text{latency}} + \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\text{floor}}} + \epsilon_{\text{margin}}$. Combines sensing-to-actuation processing latency with a certified lower bound on deceleration $a_{\text{floor}}$ and tracking margin $\epsilon_{\text{margin}}$. Serves as the fundamental geometric invariant across motion planning and safety enforcement. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-systems-stopping)

## E {#sec-glossary-vol4-e .unlisted}

**Elastic Band Trajectory Smoothing**
: A real-time trajectory deformation method that models a candidate geometric path as an elastic band subjected to internal contraction forces and external repulsive potential fields from obstacles. Modifies nominal trajectories in real time to bypass moving obstacles while preserving curvature continuity and kinematic feasibility. (@Sec-planning)

**Embodied Cognitive Deliberation**
: High-level semantic reasoning and multi-step task decomposition executed asynchronously outside hard real-time control loops. Generates symbolic goals, sub-goal poses, and task plans with latencies between 100 ms and several seconds. Decoupled from motor actuation through time-bounded leases and independent low-level kinematic planners. (@Sec-brain, @sec-intent)

**Embodied Latency Scaling Law**
: A fundamental scaling relationship governing performance improvements in physical AI policies under inference latency constraints. States that model parameter scaling yields diminishing returns unless offset by commensurate reductions in end-to-end inference latency. Excess processing delay expands stopping distances and reaction lags, eroding the task execution benefits of increased neural capacity. (@Sec-frontier)

**Embodied Shortcut Learning and Latent Epistemic Shift**
: An insidious failure mode where a policy relies on fragile simulated shortcuts or dataset artifacts that lack physical grounding in real-world deployment. The policy appears highly performant in nominal benchmark environments, but catastrophic failures emerge under small out-of-distribution shifts that break the artifact. (@Sec-frontier)

**Endogenous Covariate Shift**
: Distributional drift in sensory inputs and system states caused directly by the autonomous policy's own past actions in closed-loop operation. Distinguishes physical AI from static machine learning: an erroneous control command alters the robot's physical trajectory, altering subsequent camera viewpoints and tactile contacts, systematically shifting test-time state distributions away from training demonstrations. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-appendix-ml-compounding)

**Endogenous Feedback Loop (Action–Observation Loop)**
: The continuous, coupled cyber-physical cycle wherein digital commands actuate physical plants, changing real-world states and determining subsequent sensor readings. Links digital algorithms to physical conservation laws, time delays, and non-linear contact dynamics. Breaks open-loop statistical independence assumptions between consecutive training samples. (@Sec-boundary)

**Envelope Trichotomy**
: A runtime formal verification rule partitioning system operational status into three mutually exclusive, auditable regimes: verified inside envelope, verified outside envelope, or unknown. Both verified outside envelope and unknown strictly withhold nominal autonomous tracking authority and trigger a validated fallback maneuver, but preserve distinct diagnostic and logging signatures. (@Sec-release)

**Epipolar Line Geometry in Stereo Perception**
: The geometric constraint established between two pinhole camera views observing a 3D physical point, restricting corresponding visual features to lie along conjugate epipolar lines. Reduces stereo disparity matching from a two-dimensional planar search to a one-dimensional line search, bounding depth estimation compute latency. (@Sec-perception, @sec-appendix-systems-vision)

**EtherCAT Distributed Clocks**
: A hardware-based propagation delay compensation mechanism that synchronizes local clocks across all slave nodes on an industrial Ethernet fieldbus to sub-microsecond precision. Ensures simultaneous, jitter-free PWM update edges and encoder sampling across multi-axis robot joints. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-appendix-systems-fieldbus)

**Expected Calibration Error in Embodied Policies ($\text{ECE}$)**
: A scalar metric quantifying the alignment between a model's predicted confidence scores and empirical task success probabilities: $\text{ECE} = \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{|B_m|}{N} |\text{acc}(B_m) - \text{conf}(B_m)|$. Uncalibrated, overconfident policies fail to trigger supervisory handoffs or fallback modes prior to physical boundary violations, inducing unshielded hazard exposures. (@Sec-brain, @sec-appendix-ml-calibration)

**Expiring Intent Lease ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$)**
: A cryptographically signed or hardware-enforced permission contract granting an upstream planner authority to command the plant only within a bounded temporal window $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{start}} + \Delta t_{\text{lease}}]$. If a new valid lease is not admitted before expiration, downstream bare-metal safety supervisors immediately revoke authority and execute an autonomous stopping maneuver, preventing runaway in the event of upstream planner crashes. (@Sec-intent, @sec-planning, @sec-appendix-control-teleop-leases)

**Exposure Midpoint Timestamping (PTP)**
: The metrological practice of stamping sensor observations with the optical or physical exposure midpoint rather than the data arrival time at host memory. Employs IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol hardware timers to eliminate variable USB or PCIe transport jitter from state estimation pipelines. Essential for accurate velocity integration and multi-sensor fusion. (@Sec-data, @sec-appendix-systems-ptp)

**Extended Kalman Filter Covariance Divergence**
: A numerical or physical failure mode where an estimator's calculated error covariance matrix $\mathbf{P}_k$ becomes falsely optimistic or non-positive-definite while actual physical tracking error grows unbounded. Caused by severe unmodeled non-linearities, unobservable drift dimensions (such as wheel slip or heading drift without absolute references), or finite-precision floating-point roundoff. Bounded via Joseph-form covariance updates, covariance inflation, or observability-constrained estimators. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-control-covariance)

**Extreme Value Theory (EVT) in Tail Risk**
: A statistical framework modeling the asymptotic distribution of extreme deviations and catastrophic tail excursions rather than central means. Employs Generalized Pareto Distributions to extrapolate the probability of rare safety boundary breaches from finite physical test datasets. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-appendix-ml-evt)

## F {#sec-glossary-vol4-f .unlisted}

**Flow Matching for Continuous Actions**
: A generative modeling framework that trains continuous vector fields to transform probability distributions along optimal transport paths. Provides faster, deterministic sampling compared to standard score-based diffusion models, generating smoothed robot trajectory setpoints in fewer function evaluations. (@Sec-training, @sec-appendix-ml-diffusion)

**Forensic Authority Record**
: An immutable, tamper-resistant black-box flight recorder capturing supervisory transitions, human overrides, sensor readings, and actuator commands. Provides high-frequency, synchronized logs enabling post-incident root-cause analysis of boundary excursions or physical collisions. (@Sec-intervention)

**Forward Invariance**
: A mathematical property of a dynamical system and safe set $\mathcal{C}$ asserting that any trajectory starting within $\mathcal{C}$ remains inside $\mathcal{C}$ for all future time $t \ge 0$. Constitutes the foundational proof obligation of safety filter design; satisfied if and only if system inputs satisfy barrier conditions $\dot{h}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u}) + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0$ whenever $\mathbf{x} \in \partial \mathcal{C}$. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf)

**Four-Stage Qualification Ladder**
: A rigorous validation progression for cyber-physical AI systems spanning Model-in-the-Loop (MIL), Software-in-the-Loop (SIL), Processor-in-the-Loop (PIL), and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing. Successively integrates physical hardware components, real-time operating systems, target microcontrollers, and physical power buses to uncover timing anomalies, bus contention, and sensor noise prior to live deployment. (@Sec-verification)

**Four-Stream Action Tap**
: A data logging architecture capturing four distinct representations of every control action: requested ($a_{\text{req}}$), commanded setpoint ($a_{\text{cmd}}$), safety-enforced ($a_{\text{enf}}$), and physically measured ($a_{\text{meas}}$). Exposes actuator saturation, transmission backlash, and safety filter clipping, preventing imitation learning algorithms from fitting corrupted control signals. (@Sec-data)

**Friction Cone and Coulomb Limit**
: The geometric cone defined by the static friction coefficient $\mu$ constraining admissible tangential contact forces: $\|\mathbf{f}_t\| \le \mu f_n$. Grasping and locomotion controllers must maintain contact forces strictly within friction cones to prevent slip and loss of contact stability. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-appendix-control-contact)

**Frozen Transform Trap**
: A spatial coordinate defect where a transformation tree republishes an old geometric transform with a current, synthetic timestamp. Bypasses downstream information-age checks, causing navigation and manipulation planners to compute trajectories against dangerously stale spatial frames while assuming fresh localization. (@Sec-memory)

**Future-State Conditioning**
: A trajectory optimization and policy formulation that conditions current action selection on explicit desired future endpoint states or intermediate milestones. Anchors long-horizon motion planning while ensuring that intermediate path segments satisfy kinodynamic and collision-free feasibility constraints. (@Sec-planning)

## G {#sec-glossary-vol4-g .unlisted}

**Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) Metric Representation**
: A 3D scene parameterization that represents physical geometry and radiance as a collection of anisotropic 3D Gaussians characterized by position, orientation quaternion, scale, opacity, and spherical harmonic coefficients. Offers real-time differential rendering and metric surface reconstruction suitable for high-speed obstacle localization and policy visual grounding. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-ml-3dgs)

**Gear Ratio Scaling Law**
: Physical principles governing torque amplification and reflected inertia across mechanical gearboxes with reduction ratio $N$. Output torque scales linearly with $N$ ($\tau_{\text{out}} = N \tau_m$), while reflected rotor inertia scales quadratically ($J_{\text{refl}} = N^2 J_m$). Constrains actuator responsiveness and increases impact forces during accidental physical contact. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-rotor-jerk)

## H {#sec-glossary-vol4-h .unlisted}

**Haptic Shared Control Feedback**
: A bilateral human-machine collaboration interface that communicates automation intent and physical constraints through active forces applied directly to the operator's steering wheel or haptic joystick. Allows operators to feel virtual fixtures and safety boundaries while retaining continuous physical override authority. (@Sec-intervention)

**Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Testing**
: A real-time cyber-physical testing methodology where physical controllers, sensors, and actuators interface with high-fidelity real-time mathematical plant simulations. Evaluates real-time determinism, bus electrical loading, and fault-injection responses under extreme dynamic maneuvers without risking mechanical destruction of physical chassis. (@Sec-verification)

**Heterogeneous Silicon Partitioning**
: An architectural layout strategy that isolates safety-critical real-time control loops from non-deterministic neural inference on system-on-chip hardware. Allocates bare-metal ARM Cortex-R or Cortex-M cores for safety enforcement while assigning GPU or NPU accelerators for heavy vision and policy models, enforcing hardware memory boundaries through Memory Protection Units to prevent memory stomping. (@Sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-ipc)

**Hierarchical Whole-Body Control (WBC)**
: A multi-objective quadratic programming framework that resolves kinematically redundant joint motions by enforcing prioritized task hierarchies. Strictly satisfies higher-priority safety and contact constraints in the nullspace of subordinate manipulation or posture tasks. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-control-wbc)

**High-Order Control Barrier Function (HOCBF)**
: A generalized barrier formulation for dynamical systems where safety invariants exhibit relative degree $r \ge 2$ with respect to control inputs. Constructs recursive Lie derivative series to constrain torque and acceleration commands directly from positional safety certificates. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf)

## I {#sec-glossary-vol4-i .unlisted}

**Implicit Behavior Cloning (Energy-Based Model)**
: An imitation learning paradigm that parameterizes policies as energy functions $E(\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{a})$ over joint state-action pairs rather than direct regression mappings. Selects actions by finding energy minima at runtime: $\mathbf{a}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{a}} E(\mathbf{s}, \mathbf{a})$, naturally capturing sharp discontinuities and multi-modal demonstrator behaviors. (@Sec-training)

**Inductive Gate Delay Stretch**
: A transient microelectronic degradation where inductive voltage droop on core logic power supply rails temporarily slows transistor switching speeds. Stretches worst-case execution times and propagation delays, potentially causing setup-time violations and intermittent timing faults on overclocked embedded accelerators. (@Sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-droop)

**Inevitable Collision State (ICS)**
: A physical system state $\mathbf{x}(t)$ from which no admissible, physically executable control trajectory can prevent a collision with environmental obstacles. Evaluates complete kinodynamic limits, actuator braking capacity, and obstacle velocity bounds: $\mathbf{x} \in \text{ICS} \iff \forall \mathbf{u} \in \mathcal{U}, \, \exists t_{\text{col}} < \infty \text{ s.t. } \mathbf{x}(t_{\text{col}}) \cap \mathcal{W}_{\text{obs}}(t_{\text{col}}) \neq \emptyset$. Safety filters must intervene before the state boundary crosses into the ICS manifold. (@Sec-body, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement)

**In-Situ Physical Fault Injection**
: A qualification protocol that deliberately introduces electrical, mechanical, and sensor faults into physical hardware during operation. Tests cable disconnections, CAN bus shorts, optical lens occlusion, and thermal overload to verify that supervisory monitors detect and mitigate failures within declared safety reaction budgets. (@Sec-verification)

**Intent Grounding Refusal**
: A safety mechanism wherein a semantic task planner or vision-language-action model explicitly rejects an ambiguous, kinematically infeasible, or physically hazardous high-level user command. Halts progression to trajectory generation and returns diagnostic error tokens when prompt requests contradict physical affordance envelopes or invariant safety boundaries. (@Sec-intent)

**Intervention Masking**
: A dangerous evaluation distortion where repeated human interventions mask latent policy instability or boundary violations in benchmark tracking data. Prevents statistical estimators from observing catastrophic tail failures by resetting initial conditions before the physical crash completes, producing falsely optimistic reliability metrics. (@Sec-intervention)

**Inverse-Depth Metric Grounding**
: A geometric representation parameterizing depth as inverse distance $\rho = 1/z$ to linearize triangulation error and maintain numerical stability across distant visual features. Prevents covariance singularity when estimating scene points near the optical horizon or processing monocular visual-inertial keyframes. (@Sec-perception, @sec-appendix-systems-vision)

**Inverter Gate Drive Dead-Time Compensation**
: A timing compensation injected into motor inverter PWM gating to prevent shoot-through cross-conduction when high-side and low-side MOSFETs switch. Injects small voltage distortions and current ripple that must be compensated in firmware to preserve torque linearity at low motor speeds. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-inverters)

## J {#sec-glossary-vol4-j .unlisted}

**Jerk-Bounded Quintic Polynomial Interpolation**
: A trajectory generation method that joins kinematic waypoints using fifth-degree polynomials $s(t) = a_0 + a_1 t + \dots + a_5 t^5$. Guarantees continuity through position, velocity, and acceleration ($C^2$), producing bounded angular jerk that prevents mechanical gear shudder and inverter overcurrent trips. (@Sec-planning, @sec-appendix-control-splines)

**Joseph Form Covariance Update**
: A mathematically stabilized formulation of the Kalman filter covariance measurement update: $\mathbf{P}_{k|k} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{H}_k)\mathbf{P}_{k|k-1}(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{H}_k)^T + \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{R}_k \mathbf{K}_k^T$. Guarantees that the updated covariance matrix remains strictly positive-definite and symmetric even under finite-precision floating-point roundoff errors. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-control-covariance)

**Joule Heating and Thermal Saturation ($I^2 R$)**
: The conversion of electrical current into thermal energy within motor windings and inverter semiconductors: $P_{\text{loss}} = I^2 R_w$. Causes rapid winding temperature escalation under sustained peak torques, necessitating thermal observer models to prevent permanent demagnetization of rotor permanent magnets. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-actuators)

## K {#sec-glossary-vol4-k .unlisted}

**Kinematic Lever-Arm Error Propagation**
: The amplification of angular orientation errors into large Cartesian translation errors when transforming coordinates across long kinematic rigid linkages: $\delta \mathbf{p} = \delta \boldsymbol{\theta} \times \mathbf{r}$. A small fraction of a degree of IMU or joint encoder bias creates centimeter-scale positioning errors at the tip of an extended robotic arm, corrupting manipulation precision. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-control-spatial)

**Kinesthetic Force Feedback Lag**
: The temporal latency between slave manipulator contact force transduction and the mechanical actuation of that force at a master teleoperation console. Delays exceeding $10\text{ ms}$ degrade operator impedance perception and trigger dangerous high-frequency contact instability unless passivity controllers intervene. (@Sec-data, @sec-intervention)

**Kinodynamic Feasibility Envelope**
: The subspace of state and control space satisfying simultaneous kinematic link limits, joint range bounds, and dynamic Newton-Euler force-acceleration constraints. Restricts candidate trajectories to those that can be physically executed without exceeding joint velocity limits, actuator torque envelopes, or tipping over mobile bases. (@Sec-planning)

**KV-Cache Memory Footprint in Embodied Models**
: The DRAM storage allocated to retain key-value activation states across attention layers during autoregressive token generation in vision-language-action models. Scales linearly with context length and batch size, competing with real-time perception frame buffers for limited embedded SoC unified memory bandwidth. (@Sec-brain, @sec-placement)

## L {#sec-glossary-vol4-l .unlisted}

**Latency-Bounded Authority Handoff**
: A structured protocol that transfers control authority between autonomy and human operators within a verified temporal deadline $T_{\text{handoff}}$. Accounts for human operator sensory perception delay, cognitive re-engagement latency, and actuator ramp times. If human takeover confirmation is not received within the deadline, the supervisor immediately aborts to a minimal risk maneuver. (@Sec-intervention)

**Lie Derivative of Safety Invariants ($L_f h, L_g h$)**
: The directional derivative of a scalar barrier function $h(\mathbf{x})$ along system drift vector field $f(\mathbf{x})$ and control vector field $g(\mathbf{x})$: $L_f h(\mathbf{x}) = \nabla h(\mathbf{x}) \cdot f(\mathbf{x})$ and $L_g h(\mathbf{x}) = \nabla h(\mathbf{x}) \cdot g(\mathbf{x})$. Determines the instantaneous rate of change in safety margin produced by candidate control inputs. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf)

**Lipschitz Continuity in Policy Bounds**
: A mathematical smoothness condition bounding the maximum rate of output change relative to input perturbations: $\|\pi(\mathbf{x}_1) - \pi(\mathbf{x}_2)\| \le L_\pi \|\mathbf{x}_1 - \mathbf{x}_2\|$. In physical AI, enforcing policy Lipschitz bounds via spectral normalization prevents small sensor noise fluctuations from commanding violent, high-frequency actuator torque jerks. (@Sec-training, @sec-appendix-ml-lipschitz)

**Lock-Free Inter-Core Mailbox**
: A shared-memory communication channel connecting asymmetric CPU and MCU cores using atomic pointers and hardware memory barriers. Guarantees non-blocking setpoint transfers and event signaling without relying on OS mutexes that could cause priority inversion across heterogeneous silicon cores. (@Sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-ipc)

**Lock-Free Seqlock Buffer**
: A non-blocking shared-memory synchronization mechanism ensuring deterministic read access for hard real-time threads against asynchronous writer threads. Utilizes a monotonically increasing sequence counter: odd values signal in-flight writer mutations, while matching even values before and after reading verify that data was transferred without torn reads. Eliminates priority inversion and lock contention between neural inference and $1\,\text{kHz}$ motor loops. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-placement)

## M {#sec-glossary-vol4-m .unlisted}

**Measurement Freshness Deadline ($\Delta t_{\text{fresh}}$)**
: The maximum permissible elapsed time between physical sensor transductions and their consumption in closed-loop control feedback. Stale sensor measurements induce phase lag in feedback loops, destabilizing dynamic tracking and degrading safety margin calculations. If measurements exceed $\Delta t_{\text{fresh}}$, they are rejected as invalid. (@Sec-body, @sec-perception)

**Memory Bandwidth Wall in Edge Inference**
: The architectural throughput bottleneck where off-chip memory transfer rates limit neural accelerator utilization during low-batch autoregressive policy inference. While raw compute cores provide teraflops of throughput, weights must be transferred repeatedly from DRAM, leaving execution units starved for data. (@Sec-brain, @sec-placement)

**Memory Protection Unit (MPU) Sandboxing**
: Hardware-enforced spatial memory isolation that restricts CPU core execution and peripheral access to verified memory regions. Protects real-time safety monitor memory and peripheral registers from pointer corruption, buffer overflows, or stack stomping caused by complex perception software stacks. (@Sec-placement)

**Microarchitectural Timing Anomaly**
: A counterintuitive processor behavior where a localized execution speedup (such as an instruction cache hit) increases overall program execution latency due to out-of-order execution resource contention. Complicates hard real-time worst-case execution time analysis on high-performance superscalar embedded cores, requiring conservative qualification margins. (@Sec-placement)

**Minimal Risk Maneuver (MRM)**
: An autonomous fail-safe trajectory executed upon failure detection to bring the physical system to a low-energy, stationary safe state. Selected according to current kinematics, ranging from controlled stopping along the path to emergency braking or pulling onto an available road shoulder. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-intervention)

**Minimal-Intervention Safety Shield**
: An independent filter that tests each candidate command against a feasible input constraint derived from a validated barrier and plant model. A candidate can violate the derivative constraint while the state still has $h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$; the filter then modifies or refuses it. Solves a real-time quadratic program to minimize deviation from nominal commands subject to actuator and barrier constraints. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf)

**Mode Averaging (Multimodality Catastrophe)**
: A pathological failure of unimodal regression models trained with mean squared error on multi-modal expert demonstrations. When human demonstrators navigate around an obstacle by choosing either left or right paths, an MSE-trained network averages the behaviors, commanding a straight-line path directly into the obstacle. Resolved using diffusion policies or categorical action discretization. (@Sec-training, @sec-appendix-ml-multimodal)

**Mode Confusion (in Shared Autonomy)**
: A dangerous cognitive misalignment where a human operator's mental model of who possesses control authority contradicts the physical state of the automation system. Results in fight-the-control-wheel incidents or passive monitoring during unshielded boundary excursions; eliminated through unambiguous haptic and visual authority annunciators. (@Sec-intervention)

**Model-in-the-Loop (MIL) Simulation**
: The initial algorithmic verification phase where control logic and policy networks interact with mathematical plant models purely within numerical simulation environments. Focuses on nominal behavioral convergence, task logic, and closed-loop stability before compiling code for specific embedded runtime targets. (@Sec-verification)

**Monitored Premise Expiration**
: The automated revocation of safety case validity when real-world operational conditions deviate from the assumed design premises. Monitors friction coefficients, ambient temperature, battery degradation, and sensor packet loss rates against assumed safety bounds, transitioning system status to conditional or refusal regimes when premises fail. (@Sec-release)

**Motor Torque-Speed Operating Envelope ($S_1$ vs. $S_3$)**
: The physical boundary governing continuous versus intermittent thermal and electromagnetic torque generation across rotational velocity. Bounded by continuous torque limit $S_1$ (thermal equilibrium) and peak torque limit $S_3$ (intermittent, duration-limited before winding insulation breakdown). Constrained at high speeds by back-EMF bus voltage saturation. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-actuators)

**Multi-Rate Timing Hierarchy**
: An architectural organization that assigns distinct execution frequencies to control loops according to physical plant bandwidth and safety criticality. Typically structured as: $1\,\text{kHz}$ inner current and torque loops, $100\,\text{Hz}$ kinematics and trajectory enforcement, and $10\,\text{Hz}$ or asynchronous neural perception and semantic reasoning. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-brain)

**Multidimensional Sim-to-Real Reality Gap Vector ($\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{\text{gap}}$)**
: A quantitative vector recording systematic discrepancies across dynamics, sensing, appearance, and latency between simulated environments and the physical world. Decomposed into sub-vectors for kinematic friction $\Delta_\mu$, link inertia $\Delta_J$, sensor noise covariance $\Delta_\Sigma$, and communication delay $\Delta_\tau$. (@Sec-training)

## N {#sec-glossary-vol4-n .unlisted}

**Nagumo Forward Invariance Condition**
: A classical differential geometry condition stating that a closed set $\mathcal{C}$ is forward-invariant under system dynamics if and only if the system velocity vector field points inward or tangent to the boundary $\partial \mathcal{C}$ at every boundary point: $\dot{\mathbf{x}} \in T_{\mathcal{C}}(\mathbf{x})$. Serves as the mathematical basis for Control Barrier Function proofs. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf)

**Non-Lipschitz Contact Bifurcation**
: A sudden, discontinuous transition in physical dynamics occurring at the instant of impact or contact stick-slip transitions. Causes an infinite rate of change in contact acceleration relative to penetration depth, violating standard Lipschitz continuity assumptions required for smooth gradient propagation and classical differential equation solvers. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-appendix-control-contact)

## O {#sec-glossary-vol4-o .unlisted}

**Observation Contract ($\mathcal{O}$)**
: A formal specification defining the spatial, temporal, and semantic guarantees provided by a perception subsystem to downstream planners. Guarantees maximum latency, bounding-box confidence calibration, coordinate frame definitions, and explicit failure-indicator bits under degraded visibility. (@Sec-perception)

**Observational Indistinguishability Limit**
: A fundamental physical barrier where two distinct world states produce identical sensor telemetry within available decision time windows. Precludes any downstream software algorithm from distinguishing a safe environment from an impending collision state based on available sensor data alone. Demands conservative worst-case velocity limits or active exploratory probing. (@Sec-frontier)

**Offline-Online Evaluation Disconnect**
: The empirical divergence where high performance on static offline validation datasets fails to translate into successful closed-loop task execution on a physical robot. Caused by compounding execution errors, unmodeled sensor latencies, and closed-loop feedback effects that are absent in open-loop benchmark logs. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-appendix-ml-trajectory-distribution)

**Operating and Survival Envelopes**
: Two distinct environmental and mechanical operational boundaries defined for cyber-physical equipment. The operating envelope defines the parameter space within which the system maintains nominal task performance; the survival envelope defines the broader limits within which structural integrity is preserved without permanent plastic deformation or thermal destruction, though operations are suspended. (@Sec-verification)

**Operational Design Domain (ODD)**
: The strictly bounded set of operating conditions, environmental parameters, and roadway or facility geometries under which an autonomous system is certified to function safely. Specifies allowable weather, illumination, speed limits, surface friction ranges, and geographic geofencing boundaries outside of which autonomous operation is prohibited. (@Sec-release)

## P {#sec-glossary-vol4-p .unlisted}

**Passivity Theorem and Bounded Energy Dissipation**
: A foundational control property establishing that the feedback interconnection of two strictly passive systems is unconditionally stable. Guarantees that a robotic system interacting with arbitrary passive physical environments cannot undergo unbounded energy growth or destructive limit-cycle oscillations. (@Sec-data, @sec-appendix-control-passivity)

**Physical Artificial Intelligence (Physical AI)**
: Autonomous computational systems that combine learned perception or policy models with physical embodiments to close real-time sensory-motor loops with the physical world. Distinct from digital AI by its direct coupling to irreversible thermodynamic work, Newton's laws of motion, hardware latencies, and real-time safety constraints where algorithmic errors induce immediate physical damage. (@Sec-boundary)

**Physical AI Scope Test**
: A four-part diagnostic test verifying whether a computational system belongs to the Physical AI domain. Tests for: (1) learned perception or policy components, (2) physical embodiment exerting forces and closing feedback loops with the environment, (3) real-time deadlines where late computation is incorrect computation, and (4) irreversible physical consequences across a causal boundary. (@Sec-boundary)

**Point Cloud Sparsity and Ranging Dropouts**
: A LiDAR and depth sensor phenomenon where specular reflections, water absorption, or distant surfaces yield missing returns. Downstream spatial estimators must distinguish unobserved free space from occluded or unreflective obstacles to prevent false traversability classifications. (@Sec-perception, @sec-memory)

**Power Distribution Network (PDN) Voltage Droop Coupling**
: An electrical interference phenomenon where transient inductive voltage droop caused by high-power compute clusters destabilizes shared motor encoder or sensor rails. Mitigated through isolated DC-DC converters, dedicated star-ground power routing, and local decoupling capacitor banks. (@Sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-droop)

**Predeclared Closure Test**
: A scientific and engineering methodology requiring safety validation criteria, evaluation metrics, and test scenarios to be formally registered prior to executing empirical trials. Prevents post-hoc p-hacking, retrospective scenario cherry-picking, or subjective benchmark filtering in autonomous reliability reporting. (@Sec-frontier)

**Precision Time Protocol (IEEE 1588 PTP)**
: A network protocol providing sub-microsecond clock synchronization across distributed sensors, microcontrollers, and computing nodes over Ethernet. Employs hardware timestamping at the physical layer to eliminate operating system interrupt and packet processing jitter from multi-sensor temporal alignment. (@Sec-data, @sec-nervous, @sec-appendix-systems-ptp)

**Priority Inheritance Protocol (PIP)**
: A real-time synchronization algorithm that dynamically elevates the priority of a low-priority task holding a shared lock to match the priority of the highest-priority task blocked on that lock. Eliminates unbounded priority inversion, guaranteeing deterministic upper bounds on real-time task blocking latency. (@Sec-nervous)

**Processor-in-the-Loop (PIL) Testing**
: A verification stage where compiled production control code executes on the target embedded processor architecture while interacting with a simulated plant environment. Detects compiler optimization bugs, target instruction cache misses, floating-point rounding disparities, and microarchitectural timing delays before coupling to physical actuators. (@Sec-verification)

**Proposal–Permission Privilege Boundary**
: An architectural separation of powers dividing unverified upstream proposal generation from independent downstream permission verification. High-capacity neural networks propose candidate trajectories or actions, while a deterministic, verified safety supervisor running on an isolated core validates inputs against physical invariants before granting actuation permission. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-brain, @sec-enforcement)

## R {#sec-glossary-vol4-r .unlisted}

**Ray Frustum Voxel Lifting (Lift-Splat-Shoot)**
: A geometric transformation technique that projects 2D image features along discrete viewing rays into a 3D volumetric voxel grid. Assigns learned categorical depth distributions along each pixel ray to lift monocular visual representations into unified Bird's-Eye-View or 3D coordinate frames for spatial reasoning. (@Sec-perception, @sec-appendix-ml-patch-embedding)

**Receding-Horizon Action Chunking**
: A motion execution framework that continuously plans $K$-step action trajectories while executing only the first $M < K$ steps before re-planning with fresh observations. Balances computational efficiency with feedback responsiveness, ensuring the robot retains agility to adapt to dynamic obstacle motions. (@Sec-planning)

**Recursive Bayesian Occupancy Grid Mapping**
: A spatial representation algorithm that updates binary voxel occupancy probabilities by accumulating log-odds updates from sensor range observations: $L(m_i \mid z_{1:t}) = L(m_i \mid z_{1:t-1}) + \log \frac{p(m_i \mid z_t)}{1 - p(m_i \mid z_t)}$. Enables real-time mapping of unobserved, free, and occupied spatial cells under sensor noise. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-ml-voxels)

**Reflected Angular Jerk Limit**
: The maximum permissible rate of change in angular acceleration transmitted through an actuator gearbox. Excessive angular jerk excites mechanical torsion in gear teeth and causes micro-impacts that accelerate gearbox tooth pitting and wear. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-rotor-jerk)

**Reflected Rotor Inertia ($J_{\text{refl}}$)**
: The effective rotational inertia of an electric motor rotor as seen from the output shaft of a speed-reducing gearbox: $J_{\text{refl}} = N^2 J_m$. Scales quadratically with gear reduction ratio $N$. High reflected inertia severely restricts mechanical backdrivability, impedes high-bandwidth force control, and amplifies impact forces during unintended collisions. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-rotor-jerk)

**Regenerative Braking Energy Absorption**
: The process where decelerating electric motors act as generators, converting robot mechanical kinetic energy back into electrical current directed into the DC supply bus. Requires bus shunt capacitors or braking chopper resistors to absorb excess energy and avoid destructive overvoltage faults. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-systems-power)

**Relative Degree ($r$)**
: The number of times a scalar barrier function $h(\mathbf{x})$ must be differentiated with respect to time before the control input $\mathbf{u}$ explicitly appears: $h^{(r)} = L_f^r h + L_g L_f^{r-1} h \cdot \mathbf{u}$. For mechanical systems where safety is defined in position coordinates ($r = 2$), standard Control Barrier Functions cannot directly constrain acceleration or torque; requires high-order barrier functions to prevent safety violations. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf)

**Release Verdict Taxonomy (`PERMIT`, `COND`, `REFUSE`)**
: The formal three-valued decision output generated by a qualified safety case verification gate prior to system deployment. `PERMIT` authorizes unconditioned deployment within the verified ODD; `COND` permits deployment only under active monitoring and restricted operational envelopes; `REFUSE` strictly blocks system activation due to unsatisfied safety obligations or unmonitored hazards. (@Sec-release)

**Residual-Claims Register**
: An auditable technical document enumerating all safety claims that could not be fully substantiated through empirical evidence or formal proofs. Specifies exact unmitigated hazard mechanisms, compensatory passive protections, operational restrictions, and assigned engineering owners responsible for post-release field monitoring. (@Sec-frontier)

**Riccati Continuous Covariance Propagation**
: The continuous differential matrix equation governing state estimation error covariance evolution in Kalman-Bucy filters: $\dot{\mathbf{P}} = \mathbf{F}\mathbf{P} + \mathbf{P}\mathbf{F}^T + \mathbf{Q} - \mathbf{P}\mathbf{H}^T\mathbf{R}^{-1}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{P}$. Determines the temporal rate at which spatial confidence degrades during sensor outages. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-control-covariance)

**Rolling Shutter Distortion**
: A geometric distortion in CMOS image sensors caused by exposing rows of pixels sequentially over time rather than instantaneously. Rapid robot or obstacle motion during the frame readout interval induces shearing, warping, and perspective skew, corrupting visual feature extraction unless compensated through IMU-derived row-by-row motion unwarping. (@Sec-perception, @sec-appendix-systems-vision)

**RTOS Priority Inversion**
: A real-time scheduling hazard where a low-priority task holding a shared resource blocks a high-priority task, while an intermediate-priority task preempts the low-priority task, indefinitely delaying the high-priority deadline. Avoided in safety-critical robotics through priority inheritance protocols, priority ceiling protocols, or lock-free seqlock architectures. (@Sec-nervous)

## S {#sec-glossary-vol4-s .unlisted}

**Safe Torque Off (STO)**
: A certified hardware safety function (IEC 61800-5-2) that electronically cuts power to the motor inverter gate drivers, preventing the generation of rotational torque. Serves as the ultimate hardware-level fail-safe for emergency stops (Category 0), ensuring that no software failure or processor lockup can produce uncommanded motor movement. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-body)

**Safety Integrity Level (SIL / ASIL / AgPL)**
: A standardized metric (IEC 61508 / ISO 26262 / ISO 25119) establishing the required statistical risk reduction and target probability of dangerous hardware failures per hour. Mandates architectural redundancy, independent safety supervisors, and rigorous fault diagnosis for safety-critical control channels. (@Sec-release, @sec-verification)

**Semantic Task Invalidation**
: The runtime cancellation of an active high-level task plan caused by real-world physical changes that invalidate preconditions. For example, if a target mug to be grasped is knocked off a table mid-approach, semantic task monitors immediately invalidate the intent lease, preventing the manipulator from attempting to grasp empty air or colliding with table surfaces. (@Sec-intent)

**Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT)**
: A statistical sequential hypothesis testing procedure that evaluates whether a physical failure rate exceeds a critical threshold using minimum sample sizes. Updates a likelihood ratio after each trial and terminates testing as soon as cumulative observations cross upper (rejection) or lower (acceptance) Wald boundaries, saving thousands of testing hours compared to fixed-sample-size tests. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-appendix-ml-sprt)

**Shared Autonomy Arbitration**
: The continuous computational blending of human operator control inputs with autonomous assistance policies. Preserves human agency during high-level trajectory shaping while automatically filtering out inputs that approach kinematic singularities, collision boundaries, or actuator saturation limits. (@Sec-intervention)

**Signal Temporal Logic (STL) Quantitative Robustness**
: A formal logic framework that quantifies not only whether a cyber-physical trajectory satisfies a temporal property, but how far it is from violating it. Maps trajectory time-series to real-valued scalar robustness values $\rho^\varphi(\mathbf{x}, t)$, where positive values denote satisfaction margin and negative values indicate the magnitude of the safety violation. (@Sec-verification, @sec-appendix-ml-stl)

**Signed Fault Record (Fault Manifest)**
: A cryptographically signed data structure generated by an on-chip safety monitor when a system invariant or timing deadline is breached. Captures system state, bus logs, and register snapshots at the microsecond of failure, locking the system into a fail-safe state until qualified personnel inspect and clear the fault. (@Sec-verification)

**Silent Observation Failure**
: A sensor malfunction where a transducer outputs plausible, noise-free, but completely inaccurate measurements without asserting error flags. Common examples include frozen camera frames, biased IMU gyroscopes, or delaminated ultrasonic transducers. Detected solely through multi-sensor cross-consistency checks and dynamic residual monitoring. (@Sec-perception)

**Simplex Architecture Pattern**
: A fault-tolerant software architecture that pairs an unverified, high-performance complex controller with a formally verified, conservative safety controller. A certified safety manager continuously evaluates the state against an invariant switching boundary; if the complex controller proposes a command that threatens boundary forward invariance, the manager switches authority to the safety controller. (@Sec-enforcement)

**Sim-to-Real Contact Exploit**
: A policy learning pathology where a reinforcement learning agent exploits numerical penetration or non-physical contact artifacts in physics simulation to achieve high rewards. Policies that exploit integrator energy pumps or spring-damper interpenetration fail catastrophically when deployed on physical mechanisms governed by true non-penetration constraints. (@Sec-training, @sec-appendix-control-contact)

**Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) Simulation**
: A virtual testing environment where production application software runs on developer workstations inside containerized emulators connected to software physics engines. Enables massive parallel execution of regression test suites and scenario fuzzing without requiring dedicated target embedded hardware. (@Sec-verification)

**Spatial Belief Contract**
: A formal guarantee governing spatial state estimation, defining valid volume bounds, maximum covariance ellipsoid diameters, and coordinate frame consistency. Downstream motion planners verify the belief contract before utilizing occupancy maps; if covariance grows beyond declared bounds, planners trigger active exploratory sensing or reduce velocity. (@Sec-memory)

**Spatial Information Age ($\tau_{\text{age}}$)**
: The elapsed duration between the physical exposure or measurement epoch of a spatial observation and the current execution epoch: $\tau_{\text{age}} = t_{\text{curr}} - t_{\text{capture}}$. Expands the effective volume of obstacles to account for unobserved motion during the delay interval: $r_{\text{eff}} = r_{\text{obs}} + v_{\text{obs,max}} \tau_{\text{age}}$. (@Sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-appendix-systems-stopping)

**Spline Seam ($C^2$)**
: A quintic or Hermite trajectory segment designed to join two independently planned motion chunks with continuous position, velocity, and acceleration. Enforcing continuity through the second derivative ($\ddot{\mathbf{x}}(t^-) = \ddot{\mathbf{x}}(t^+)$) guarantees bounded motor torque rates, preventing mechanical gear shudder and inverter trips. (@Sec-planning, @sec-appendix-control-splines)

**Stopping Suffix ($C^2$)**
: A pre-computed, dynamically feasible braking trajectory permanently reserved at the end of every active motion chunk. Ensures that if an upstream planner fails to deliver a new valid chunk before the current lease expires, the robot decelerates smoothly to a complete standstill without violating kinematic or barrier constraints. (@Sec-planning)

**Support Envelope Relational Join**
: A data indexing operation that correlates high-frequency robot telemetry streams (such as joint torques and motor currents) with low-frequency multimodal camera observations based on precise PTP timestamps. Ensures that imitation learning datasets maintain exact causal correspondence between visual states and resulting control actions. (@Sec-data)

## T {#sec-glossary-vol4-t .unlisted}

**Tactile Sensor Shear and Normal Decoupling**
: The spatial and algorithmic separation of normal compressive contact forces from tangential shear forces in optical or elastomeric tactile arrays. Critical for detecting incipient slip during precision manipulation prior to total grasp failure. (@Sec-perception, @sec-body)

**Takeover Reaction Budget ($T_{\Sigma}$)**
: The total temporal allocation required for a human supervisor to perceive an alert, transition cognitive attention, evaluate the physical scene, and execute an evasive manual input: $T_{\Sigma} = T_{\text{alert}} + T_{\text{cognition}} + T_{\text{motor}} + T_{\text{plant}}$. Defines the minimum warning lead-time that autonomous safety monitors must provide before an imminent boundary violation occurs. (@Sec-intervention)

**Target-Evidence Horizon ($\tau_{\text{evidence}}$)**
: The maximum time interval an autonomous system is permitted to pursue a visually occluded or unobserved target before confirming its continued physical presence. Mitigates hallucination in vision-language models by enforcing target re-acquisition checks before high-force physical interactions are initiated. (@Sec-intent)

**Task Tolerance Envelope**
: The allowable spatial, velocity, and force error bounds within which a manipulation or navigation task is considered successfully executing. If tracking error exceeds this envelope, the system immediately suspends open-loop chunk execution and re-evaluates high-level intent. (@Sec-intent)

**Teleoperation Round-Trip Latency ($t_{\text{loop}}$)**
: The total elapsed time for sensor data to travel from the robot across network links to the operator console and for operator control commands to return to robot actuators: $t_{\text{loop}} = t_{\text{uplink}} + t_{\text{operator}} + t_{\text{downlink}}$. Round-trip delays exceeding approximately $100\text{ ms}$ degrade human teleoperation stability, inducing operator-induced oscillations unless mitigated through predictive displays or wave-variable passivity controllers. (@Sec-data, @sec-appendix-control-teleop-leases)

**Temporal Ensembling**
: A post-processing technique for action chunking where overlapping trajectory predictions generated at successive time steps are blended via exponential or linear weighting. Smooths inter-chunk discontinuities, filters high-frequency policy noise, and stabilizes closed-loop execution without incurring the latency cost of single-step re-planning. (@Sec-brain, @sec-training)

**Thermal-Timing Clock Throttling**
: A hardware protection mechanism where processor clock frequencies are dynamically reduced to prevent thermal damage when junction temperatures exceed thermal limits. Sudden throttling expands software execution times, transforming normally safe code into late, deadline-missing failures on hard real-time control buses. (@Sec-placement)

**Thermodynamic Irreversibility in Actuation**
: The fundamental physical principle that mechanical work performed on the external environment dissipates thermal energy and induces entropy changes that cannot be computationally reversed. Marks the strict boundary where software idempotence ceases to apply. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-body)

**Tightly Coupled Memory (TCM)**
: High-speed, single-cycle SRAM integrated directly alongside embedded real-time processor execution pipelines. Bypasses shared SoC caches and bus crossbars, eliminating cache-miss latency jitter for microsecond-critical interrupt service routines and safety filter checks. (@Sec-placement, @sec-nervous)

**Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN / IEEE 802.1Qbv)**
: A suite of IEEE Ethernet standards enabling deterministic, scheduled message transport over standard physical Ethernet infrastructure. Implements time-aware traffic shapers and gate drivers that guarantee scheduled time slots for critical motor control packets while isolating best-effort video streaming traffic. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-appendix-systems-fieldbus)

**Time-to-Harm ($t_{\text{harm}}$)**
: The minimum physical time required for the current kinematic state to evolve into an irreversible collision, structural failure, or human injury under worst-case disturbances: $t_{\text{harm}} = \inf \{ t > 0 \mid \mathbf{x}(t) \in \mathcal{X}_{\text{hazard}} \}$. Must remain strictly greater than the system's worst-case stopping reaction time ($t_{\text{harm}} > \tau_{\text{reaction}} + \tau_{\text{brake}}$) to guarantee safe operation. (@Sec-frontier)

**Time-Triggered Architecture (TTA)**
: A system design paradigm where all computation, communication, and actuation activities are initiated at predetermined, synchronized clock ticks rather than in response to asynchronous events. Eliminates dynamic resource contention, buffer overflows, and priority inversions, providing mathematically verifiable determinism for ultra-dependable systems. (@Sec-nervous)

**Trajectory Record**
: A timestamped sequence of kinematic states, control inputs, and constraint satisfaction flags recorded across a planned or executed motion path. Serves as the ground-truth reference for tracking controllers, compliance monitors, and post-execution path optimization. (@Sec-planning)

**Transmission Backlash and Compliance**
: Mechanical deadband and elastic structural flexure in gear teeth, timing belts, and harmonic drives. Introduces non-collocated sensor dynamics where motor encoder positions depart from true link positions, degrading endpoint manipulation accuracy. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-control-flexible-joints)

**Truncated Signed Distance Function (TSDF) Fusion**
: A 3D volumetric mapping algorithm that represents surface geometry by storing the signed distance to the nearest physical surface inside regular voxel grids, truncated beyond a narrow band. Fuses successive depth observations using weighted running averages, achieving millimeter-scale surface reconstruction while filtering high-frequency sensor noise. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-ml-spatial)

**Two-Speed Embodied Compute Architecture**
: An architectural design pattern that partitions physical AI processing into an asynchronous, high-latency deliberative loop ($1\text{--}10\,\text{Hz}$) and a synchronous, hard real-time reactive enforcement loop ($100\text{--}1000\,\text{Hz}$). The deliberative loop processes vision-language-action models and semantic plans on high-power system-on-chips, while the reactive loop enforces barrier certificates, evaluates dynamic stopping distances, and commands motor inverters on certified microcontrollers. (@Sec-brain, @sec-placement)

## U {#sec-glossary-vol4-u .unlisted}

**Unannounced Fault Injection**
: A black-box verification protocol where physical or software faults are injected into the operational system without triggering diagnostic warnings in the test harness beforehand. Tests whether autonomous monitoring systems detect and mitigate latent hardware faults purely from environmental and physical telemetry under live operating conditions. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-verification)

**Unilateral Contact Constraint**
: A physical kinematic boundary condition specifying that solid bodies cannot interpenetrate and can only exert compressive (pushing), non-adhesive normal forces: $g_N(\mathbf{q}) \ge 0, \, \lambda_N \ge 0, \, g_N \lambda_N = 0$. Governs all physical grasping, locomotion, and tool manipulation. Introduces non-smooth complementarity dynamics that challenge classical continuous control theory. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-appendix-control-contact)

**Unobservable Subspace Drift**
: The unbounded accumulation of state estimation error along state space dimensions that produce no measurable changes in sensor observations. For example, yaw drift in IMU-only odometry on flat terrain or absolute position drift in wheel encoder integration during continuous wheel slip. Requires periodic re-anchoring to global spatial landmarks. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-control-covariance)

## V {#sec-glossary-vol4-v .unlisted}

**Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Intent Translation**
: An end-to-end multimodal foundation model architecture that consumes natural language instructions and visual observations to directly predict robot action tokens. Connects high-level human semantic concepts to low-level motor primitives, requiring runtime grounding filters to ensure proposed token actions satisfy physical workspace limits. (@Sec-intent, @sec-brain)

**Volumetric Free-Space Raycasting**
: A ray-tracing operation through 3D spatial voxel grids that decrements occupancy log-odds along sensor sightlines up to the measured obstacle distance. Explicitly clears previously occupied space when obstacles move, allowing real-time mapping systems to adapt to dynamic environments while preserving safe clearance margins. (@Sec-memory, @sec-appendix-ml-voxels)

## W {#sec-glossary-vol4-w .unlisted}

**Watchdog Validity Lease ($T_{\text{lease}}$)**
: A hardware- or timer-enforced validity window within which an autonomous controller must refresh a physical heartbeat signal. If the heartbeat or fresh command is not written to the watchdog register before $T_{\text{lease}}$ elapses, the watchdog circuit asserts a hardware reset or triggers safe torque off, halting the machine. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-timers)

**Wave-Variable Passivity**
: A mathematical control transformation that guarantees stability in bilateral teleoperation over arbitrary, unknown network time delays. Encodes velocity and force signals into power-conjugate wave variables: $u = \frac{F + b \dot{x}}{\sqrt{2b}}, \, v = \frac{F - b \dot{x}}{\sqrt{2b}}$. Preserves passivity by ensuring that communication delay cannot generate fictitious energy that would destabilize the mechanical plant. (@Sec-data, @sec-appendix-control-passivity)

**Wheel Slip Ratio**
: The dimensionless normalized velocity discrepancy between tire surface rotational velocity and vehicle longitudinal ground velocity: $\lambda_{\text{slip}} = \frac{\omega r - v_x}{\max(\omega r, v_x)}$. When slip ratio exceeds peak friction adhesion thresholds, available lateral steering force collapses, leading to vehicle spinout or loss of odometry observability. (@Sec-body, @sec-appendix-control-slip)

**Windowed Watchdog Timer (WWDT)**
: A specialized hardware timer that requires a heartbeat service write to occur not only before an expiration deadline, but strictly after a minimum window duration. Detects both frozen software tasks (too late) and runaway loops or premature interrupt triggering (too early), providing dual-boundary execution integrity checks. (@Sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-timers)

**Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET)**
: A mathematically or empirically certified upper bound on the time required to execute a specific software task on a dedicated target processor. Serves as the bedrock parameter for real-time schedulability analysis such as rate monotonic scheduling. Must account for pipelining, cache misses, and bus interference to guarantee that safety filter deadlines are met under all operational conditions. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-timers)

## Z {#sec-glossary-vol4-z .unlisted}

**Zero-Allocation SRAM Invariant**
: A hard real-time software design constraint prohibiting dynamic memory allocation (`malloc`, `free`, or runtime heap instantiation) during cyclic execution loops. Pre-allocates all trajectory buffers, solver workspaces, and state caches in static, tightly coupled SRAM prior to entering the control loop. Eliminates heap fragmentation, garbage collection delays, and non-deterministic memory allocation failures. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement)

**Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) Phase Lag**
: The effective phase delay introduced when continuous control commands are updated at discrete sampling intervals $T_s$: $G_{\text{zoh}}(s) = \frac{1 - e^{-s T_s}}{s}$, approximating an effective time delay of $T_s / 2$. Reduces feedback phase margins, constraining the maximum achievable closed-loop control bandwidth in digital motor inverters. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-appendix-control-zoh)
